blogs.title: When Three Valves Aren’t Enough: Managing TAV‑in‑TAV‑in‑TAV Failures
blogs.description: A deep dive into the technical and anatomic challenges of a third‑generation transcatheter valve implantation. We’ll explore CT‑based sizing, frame‑to‑frame interaction, coronary obstruction risk, commissural alignment strategies, and how to preserve effective orifice area in a triple‑stented aortic root.

blogs.title: Prosthetic Valve Endocarditis Meets TAVR: When is a Redo TAVR Safe?
blogs.description: Examines the evidence and guideline nuances for using TAVR after treated prosthetic valve endocarditis. Discusses infection control checkpoints, timing of re‑intervention, antimicrobial stewardship, and risk‑benefit analysis versus surgical explant in high‑risk patients.

blogs.title: Lifetime Planning for Structural Valve Disease: From First TAVR to the Third
blogs.description: Focuses on the concept of “valve‑in‑valve stewardship.” How to anticipate future re‑interventions at the index procedure, choose valve platforms that facilitate later access, and use pre‑procedural imaging to map a patient’s procedural trajectory over decades.

blogs.title: Coronary Access After Multiple TAVR Layers: Imaging, Techniques, and Future Options
blogs.description: Analyzes coronary re‑access after serial TAVR procedures. Reviews CT metrics (coronary ostial height, sinus dimensions, valve‑to‑coronary distance), commissural alignment tools, and adjunctive strategies like BASILICA, valve fracture, or dedicated coronary‑friendly devices.

blogs.title: Patient‑Prosthesis Mismatch in Redo TAVR: Hemodynamics, Device Choice, and Post‑Dilatation Tactics
blogs.description: Explores why severe gradients can persist after a third valve and how careful device selection, high implantation, and aggressive post‑dilatation can mitigate PPM. Includes a review of hemodynamic data from the case and practical algorithms for similar patients.

blogs.title: Vascular Complications in Serial TAVR: Lessons from a Post‑Procedural Femoral Pseudoaneurysm
blogs.description: Uses the patient’s femoral pseudoaneurysm after the second TAVR to discuss access site selection, vessel preparation, closure device choice, and bailout surgical options. Highlights how cumulative vascular trauma influences planning for subsequent trans‑catheter procedures.
